Fenmoor Digital - agency weekly report, week 43 (published Monday 26 October 2026). Lead project for this issue: Kittiwake, the direct-booking engine we are building for Seacliff Resorts. The rest of the client portfolio follows.

Kittiwake for Seacliff Resorts
What it is: a booking engine for Seacliff's four coastal hotels, replacing the third-party widget that charges 4 percent per booking. Scope covers room search, rate plans, packages with spa treatments, card payments, and a confirmation flow that writes into Seacliff's property-management system. Agreed launch: November 30, before the winter-break booking season.

Progress this week
Raj and Elif finished the rate-plan engine, including the length-of-stay discounts Seacliff's revenue manager asked for. The property-management interface now writes bookings and cancellations correctly in the vendor's test environment. Accessibility review of the search page found six issues; four are fixed.

Client decision
On October 21 Seacliff's managing director wrote to us formally. Seacliff has been acquired by the Larchmont hotel group, which runs its own central reservations platform across all its properties, and Seacliff is required to move onto it. Seacliff is therefore ending the Kittiwake engagement under clause 14 of the contract: the booking engine will not be launched, and we are to stop work at the end of October. They will pay for work completed to that date plus the agreed wind-down fee. We have acknowledged the letter, and Raj and Elif are writing hand-over notes so Larchmont can see how the rate plans were modelled.

Other clients
- Thornbury Museum: the new collections website launched on October 20. Traffic is up 30 percent and the donate button has already raised more in a week than the old site did in a month.
- Atlas Cycles: the e-commerce migration is two weeks late because their product data export keeps failing. New launch date December 7; the team keeps building the checkout in the meantime.

- Hollin Brewery: their loyalty app was cancelled by the brewery in September; final invoice paid last week.

Studio

Finance
October revenue is tracking at 96 percent of forecast. Accounts receivable over 60 days: one invoice from Atlas Cycles, which they have promised to pay this week.

People

Coming up
Pitch to a regional theatre group on November 4. Studio closed on November 11 for the team day out.

Today: 2026-09-02
PRD - Pinecrest patient portal: online appointment self-scheduling. Milestone review, 2 September 2026. This PRD covers the self-scheduling project for the Pinecrest Health portal; other portal workstreams appear in the dependencies section.

Problem
About 62 percent of calls to Pinecrest's central booking line are routine appointment requests that could be handled online. Average wait on the line was 11 minutes in July. Patients can already see their upcoming appointments in the portal but cannot book, move or cancel them without phoning.

Goals
- Patients can book follow-up and routine visits with their own care team in primary care, dermatology and physiotherapy.
- Patients can reschedule or cancel up to 24 hours before a visit.
- Reduce booking-line call volume by 25 percent within six months.

Contract and deadline
Pinecrest's agreement with the regional health authority funds the project on condition that self-scheduling is live for all primary-care clinics by September 30, 2026.

Design
The booking flow was usability-tested with 20 patients, including six over 70 and three screen-reader users. Median time to book was 2 minutes 10 seconds. The main change after testing was to show the clinician's photo next to each slot, which older patients said reassured them.

Integration with the EHR
Self-scheduling reads open slots and writes bookings through the EHR vendor's scheduling API version 3, which adds the visit-type rules our clinics rely on. The vendor committed to delivering v3 to Pinecrest's test environment on August 3. The vendor delivered v3 on August 3 as committed; our integration tests passed on August 14 and the end-to-end test with three pilot clinics finished on August 28 with no open defects. Primary-care go-live for all clinics is booked for September 22, eight days before the funding deadline, with dermatology and physiotherapy following in October as planned.

Milestones
M1 Design complete - June 30 (done).
M2 Portal front end complete - July 31 (done).
M3 EHR integration and pilot clinics - August 31.
M4 All primary-care clinics - by September 30.
M5 Dermatology and physiotherapy - October.

Dependencies on other portal workstreams
- Portal login modernisation (passkeys): delayed until November because of a browser-compatibility issue; self-scheduling works with the current login.
- Prescription refill requests: on hold while pharmacy reviews its controlled-substances policy; independent of scheduling.
- Video-visit integration: cancelled in July after Pinecrest chose a different telehealth vendor that has its own booking.
- SMS reminders: live since June, and will cover self-booked appointments automatically.

Metrics
We will track the share of eligible appointments booked online, call volume to the booking line, no-show rates for online versus phone bookings, and patient satisfaction in the post-booking survey.

Risks
Clinics with complex visit-type rules may expose gaps in the v3 rule engine; the pilot clinics were chosen to include the two most complex ones. Some patients may book the wrong visit type; the flow asks a short triage question first.

Owners
Product: Lucia Hernandez. Engineering: Darnell Price. Clinical lead: Dr. Yuki Sato. EHR liaison: Tomasz Wrobel.
